name: Voltaic Resonance Disruptor VRD-3 'Livewire'
description:
The Voltaic Resonance Disruptor operates by generating a tuned electromagnetic carrier wave that couples directly with the bioelectric field of living targets. Developed under ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's 'Project Harmonic' initiative, the VRD-3 emits a modulated burst that oscillates at frequencies specifically calibrated to interfere with sodium-potassium ion exchange across cell membranes. The result is a cascading depolarization event that spreads outward from the point of initial contact like a stone dropped in still water, disrupting voluntary motor function without causing immediate tissue death.

What distinguishes the VRD-3 from cruder electroshock platforms is its precision tuning system — a rotating dial on the receiver allows operators to shift the resonance band between incapacitation, sustained agony, and lethal cardiac interference. This tunability earned the weapon considerable interest from both law enforcement contractors and private security firms, though the lethal setting has since been restricted under GLMZ's Bioelectric Harm Ordinance 7.4. Field technicians have long known that a simple hardware bypass restores full-spectrum functionality, and modification kits circulate freely in the lower districts.

The weapon's distinctive high-pitched harmonic whine during charge-up — colloquially called 'singing' — has made it impossible to deploy with any element of surprise. Experienced street operators have learned to exploit this: the sound alone is often enough to provoke compliance before a shot is ever fired. In the Shunt district, a drawn Livewire is understood as a social ultimatum.
specifications:
effective range: 18m (optimal), 30m (degraded)
charge time: 1.4 seconds
power source: ZHENG-DAO ZD-7 Galvanic Cell (12 shots per cell)
weight: 1.9 kg
length: 34 cm
settings: Incapacitation, Sustained Pain, Lethal (restricted)
resonance bands: 40 Hz – 220 Hz adjustable
housing: Matte polymer over conductive internal cage
tactical_use: Preferred in close-quarters detention and crowd suppression. Security operators typically use the incapacitation band to drop targets without lethal liability, then transition to physical restraint. Corporate extraction teams use modified units with the lethal band enabled for quiet termination operations where ballistic evidence must be avoided. The weapon's limited range makes it poorly suited for open engagements; operators typically close distance using cover before deploying.
cultural_context: The Livewire has become a class symbol in GLMZ — specifically, a symbol of institutional violence with plausible deniability. Corporate security personnel carry them openly as a statement of licensed authority. In the lower districts, possessing an unmodified VRD-3 signals someone with corporate ties or aspirations. A modified unit, by contrast, signals someone who has cut those ties and doesn't care who knows it. Street medics have developed protocols specifically for treating resonance cascade injuries, which they call 'singing sickness.'
known_users: Modified-unit carriers in the Shunt district underworld
story_hooks: A ZHENG-DAO whistleblower claims the VRD-3's lethal band was never actually restricted — only the documentation was changed. She has internal firmware logs to prove it.
A string of deaths in the Velour District show all the biological markers of cardiac resonance failure, but no VRD-3s are recovered at any scene. Someone is using an undetectable delivery method.
The modification kits flooding the market are suspiciously uniform — same machining tolerances, same component sourcing. Someone is manufacturing them at scale and distributing them deliberately.

A licensed security operator's VRD-3 spontaneously shifted to lethal band during a routine detention, killing the subject. The operator swears they never touched the dial. ZHENG-DAO is quietly buying the case files.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular energy weapon with a distinctly organic curve to its receiver. The VRD-3 resembles a marriage between a stun baton and a precision instrument — aggressive yet clinical. The barrel is not a traditional muzzle but rather a resonance emitter array, a honeycomb of conductive apertures arranged in a widening funnel. The overall silhouette is compact and forward-weighted, designed for one-handed tactical deployment.
physical_description.dimensions: 34 cm length overall; 8 cm width at the widened emitter head; 6 cm depth at grip; emitter array spans 5 cm diameter
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced — 1.9 kg distributed toward the emitter creates a natural pointing tendency. Feels purposeful in hand, never awkward, despite the asymmetrical geometry.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte polymer composite frame over a conductive internal cage of copper-nickel lattice; emitter head is reinforced titanium-edged ceramic
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer body with a subtle industrial texture to prevent slip. The conductive cage visible through translucent sections of the housing glows faintly under certain light. Emitter apertures have a brushed metallic finish that catches light in nested patterns.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal matte primary; gunmetal gray conductive elements; accent lines in electric cyan running along the spine of the receiver and framing the power indicator
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with shallow grip channels; slightly tacky rubberized surface for retention even in wet conditions. The trigger guard is oversized and angular, designed for gloved operation.
distinctive_features: Rotating resonance-tuning dial on the left receiver side, marked with frequency bands in small luminescent numerals
Honeycomb-pattern emitter array at the barrel, flared like a speaker horn
Power indicator LED strip running along the spine — cycles from blue (charged) to white (peak resonance) to amber (decay)
Faint geometric etching along the grip depicting harmonic wave patterns
Capacitor charging nodes visible as raised titanium nodes along the internal cage visible through translucent housing sections
Micro-vent ports along the rear receiver to dissipate resonance bleed-off
ZHENG-DAO serial plate mounted on the right side of the grip in microdot format
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC logo (stylized sine wave) embossed on the grip; 'VRD-3 LIVEWIRE' designation in small block lettering above the trigger; model serial number in microdot on right receiver panel; 'INCAPACITATION MODE STANDARD CONFIGURATION' warning stamp in three languages on the power cell bay
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained units show minimal wear; the matte finish masks micro-scratches well. Field-used units develop scorching marks around the emitter apertures from resonance bleed, discoloration in cyan-to-amber gradients. Modified units (with lethal setting restored) often show evidence of hastily re-soldered circuit traces near the tuning dial; the thermal stress creates subtle warping in the plastic housing that marks it to trained eyes. Street units in the lower tiers show pitting in the emitter ceramic and burn marks along the vent ports.
